definition: A quest whose only job is to send you to another NPC or hub; small XP, worth it only when the destination is already on your route.
A series of quests where each unlocks the next; judge it by the total XP per minute of the parts on your route, not by the first part.
A cluster of quest givers (town, camp or outpost) where you accept and turn in several quests at once.
A circuit that leaves a hub, completes several quests' objectives and returns (often by hearth) to turn them all in.
A mob at or below your gray level; it gives no XP. Gray level is level - floor(level/10) - 5 below 40 and level - floor(level/5) - 1 from 40.
The color of a mob's level: gray (no XP), green (below you, reduced XP), yellow (about your level), orange (2-4 above), red (5+ above), skull (far above or boss).
Hitting a mob first so its kill credit and loot belong to you (and your group); an untagged kill by someone else gives you nothing.
Progress on a kill objective; in a group every member in range who has the quest gets it.
Using the Hearthstone to teleport to the inn you are bound to (10 s cast).
Setting your Hearthstone's destination at an innkeeper; the guide's .home steps say where.
The Hearthstone's 60-minute cooldown (Classic, and observed on the Forever beta); it keeps ticking while you are logged out.
A Classic Era trick that binds a new inn and still hearths to the old one by finishing both in the same server batch; unverified on Forever.
Rested XP: a pool that doubles kill XP until it is used up; builds while logged out (5% of a level per 8 h in an inn or capital, a quarter of that elsewhere, cap 150% of a level).
The point on the XP bar up to which kills pay double; quest XP moves it forward, kills consume up to it.
A rested area with an innkeeper; logging out there is instant and builds rest at the full rate.
Reaching the next level.
Experience earned per hour of play, the coach's main pace measure; compared against a level-band benchmark.
Killing mobs for XP rather than quest objectives; used as filler to meet an XP gate.
A level or XP amount the guide requires before the next section (RestedXP .xp steps), because the next quests need it.
Leaving a zone once you out-level it or finish its useful quests, moving to the next zone in the route.
Dying on purpose so the spirit healer resurrects you at a graveyard near your destination; RestedXP .deathskip steps, softcore only.
Resurrecting at the spirit healer instead of running to your corpse; costs 25% durability and resurrection sickness from level 11.
Running back to your body as a ghost (125% run speed, nothing attacks you) to resurrect without sickness.
Resurrection Sickness: -75% stats and damage after a spirit res; none at 1-10, (level - 10) minutes at 11-19, 10 minutes from 20.
Item condition; dying costs 10% on equipped items, a spirit res 25% more, and items at 0% give no stats.
How close you can get before a hostile mob attacks: about 20 yards at equal level, about 1 yard more or less per level of difference.
Nearby mobs of the same kind joining a fight when one is pulled.
A 4-second 50% slow (and dismount) from melee hits landing on your back while you move away; chance up to 40%, lower under level 30.
Starting a fight with one or more mobs, ideally at a time and place you choose.
An extra mob that joins a fight you started with fewer.
Line of sight; breaking it (stepping behind a wall) forces casters and ranged mobs to walk to you.
Keeping a mob chasing you while you damage it from range, using slows and movement.
A mob giving up and returning to its spawn after being pulled too far.
A mob that walks a route; check its path before pulling near it.
A killed mob or object reappearing; most open-world mobs take minutes, named quest mobs often longer.
A mob with a gold dragon frame: roughly 2-3x the health and damage of a normal mob; gives double XP.
Kill XP for an elite: twice a normal mob of the same level.
A rare-spawn mob (silver dragon) with better loot and a long respawn; worth killing only if it's on the path.
Flight path: a flight master node; both ends must be discovered to fly between them.
A ship between ports (e.g. Menethil-Auberdine, Booty Bay-Ratchet); docks for 60 s and cycles in about 3-5 minutes.
The Horde (and Forever Skyborne) airship between ports; same 60 s dock and 3-5 minute cycle as boats.
A quest only your class can take, usually rewarding a spell, form, pet or class item.
A quest meant for several players (often elite targets); solo only if you out-level it.
A quest where an NPC walks a route that you must protect; slow and can fail.
Handing a completed quest to its NPC to get the XP and reward.
A quest you must complete before another becomes available.
One of two or more quests where taking one locks the others out.
Reduced quest XP when you out-level a quest: full up to quest level +5, then 80/60/40/20% at +6/+7/+8/+9 and 10% from +10.
ZD: the level gap below you at which a mob's XP reaches zero in the kill-XP formula (5 at 1-7, 8 at 12-15, 11 at 20-29, 12 at 30-39, 16 at 55-59).
The maximum number of quests you can hold: 20 in Classic (Forever's cap not yet verified).
Time not killing or travelling: eating, drinking, bandaging, waiting for respawns.
The order of abilities you use in a fight; while leveling, the cheapest one that kills fast.
Global cooldown: the ~1.5 s (1 s for energy users) lockout after most abilities.
Warrior and bear resource: earned by dealing and taking damage, decays out of combat.
Rogue and cat resource: 100 max, refills about 10 per second.
Caster resource; Spirit-based regen pauses for 5 s after each spell (the five-second rule).
Spirit mana regeneration stops for 5 seconds after you cast a spell; finishing with a wand or melee restarts it sooner.
Secondary profession for bandages: ~6-8 s channel, interrupted by damage, 60 s Recently Bandaged lockout.
Secondary profession for food; some RestedXP quests need Cooking 10 or 50, and on Forever it builds campfires and buff food.
Food that gives a Well Fed buff after 10 s of eating; RestedXP's Forever guides say any buff food adds 5% kill XP for 15 minutes (unverified).
Skill with a weapon type, max 5x level; low skill means misses and glancing blows, and it rises quickly on easy mobs.
Capital-city trainer who teaches new weapon types for 10 silver (polearms 1 gold at 20).
Being allowed to equip an armor or weapon type at all (e.g. plate at 40 in Classic; RestedXP's Forever rules say 35).
Bound to you; can't be traded or sold on the auction house, only vendored.
Bind on Equip: tradeable until worn, so it can be sold on the auction house.
Gray items with no use except vendor gold.
Auction house in capital cities; only worth visiting when you're already there.
Leveling to 60 in the least /played time, measured in days and hours played.
/played time at milestone levels (10, 20, 30...) used to compare a run with a benchmark or record.
Total time played on the character, the speedrun clock.
Pulling many mobs and killing them together with area spells (classically frost mages with Blizzard from ~22).
Gaining levels by running instances with a group; on Forever dungeon kill XP is reduced and quests carry the XP, so one quest run per dungeon.
A high-level player killing dungeon mobs for a low-level one; on Forever reduced dungeon kill XP makes it weaker.
A group of AoE casters clearing big pulls together in dungeons.
WoW Forever's new race: Alliance High Order or Horde Windshaper; Warrior, Hunter, Rogue, Druid, plus Mage (Alliance) or Shaman (Horde).
The Skyborne starting island, roughly levels 1-12 (RestedXP's route runs it 1-14), with windstone crystals and speed-boosting tornadoes.
Skyborne racial: a 10-second glide, useful for dropping off cliffs on your path.
Forever camp centre built with Cooking; sitting near it for a minute grants Camp Benefits; lasts about 10 minutes.
Forever buff from sitting at a camp for a minute; combines the effects of placed camp objects, which don't stack with class buffs.
Forever camp effect tied to rested XP from a camp; shown as a debuff that blocks repeat use for about an hour (effect size unverified).
Forever quests (one per trained profession, at skill 20) that teach a camp object for that profession.
Forever starter quest (~level 5-6): /sit at a campfire until Boosted Rest appears; relog if it doesn't.
Forever account progression system with perks such as Well Rested (bigger, faster rested XP); access around level 25.
The leveling guide addon the player follows; its steps encode route, XP gates, hearths and deathskips.
One line of a RestedXP guide (accept, turn in, kill, go to, hearth...); the coach tracks the current step.
A RestedXP step that stays active across later steps until its objective is done (#sticky).
A RestedXP step marked #optional: marginal, skip it when behind pace or if it isn't available.
RestedXP #completewith: do this objective in the background while following the next steps, until the named later step.
Logging out at certain guide-marked spots so the server places you outside a cave or structure when you log back in.
A precise mountain route that saves a long walk without dying (e.g. Dun Morogh to Wetlands).
Ranged weapon for priests, mages and warlocks that costs no mana; a large share of their leveling damage.
Class trainer who sells new spells and ranks, added at even levels in Classic.
One point per level from 10, spent in the talent trees; respecs get more expensive each time.
60% speed riding mount at 40 in Classic (100 gold total); on Forever the mount comes with riding training and the price is unannounced.
A mob RestedXP's database flags for special abilities, patrols or high damage (charges, nets, stuns, heals).
Many humanoids run at about 15-20% health and can bring friends back.
